failing.summary: internal/surface/cli/guard.go:124 (raised by opus): Claim (guard check --help, mirrored in the generated docs/reference/cli/commands.md:1308-1313): what an allow 'still does not see' includes 'a parameter expansion that carries no substitution ($VAR, ${VAR:-git}) wherever it stands — as the program's name, as a flag, or inside an interpreter payload ... because the guard sees the variable, not what the shell expands it to'. Reality: this release reads a value the same line assigns and then uses (CHANGELOG.md:24, commands/guard.md:272-289). The binary blocks `P=pkill; $P make` and `X='rm -rf /'; sh -c "$X"` (guard check exit 1 for both), so the help text now under-states what the guard reads. The text is unchanged since v0.14.0 while the behaviour changed. It fails safe, because the guard blocks more than the help says, so a user is not led into a dangerous action. Smallest fix: in guard.go qualify the clause as 'a parameter expansion of a variable the line does not itself assign (`$VAR`, ...)', then run `go generate ./internal/surface/cli` so commands.md follows.

failing.summary: CHANGELOG.md:47 (raised by opus): Claim: masking covers 'the reasons, titles and records `drain`, `capture list` and `capture status` show'. Reality: abcd has no `capture status` sub-verb. The `abcd capture --help` list has admit, defer, disposition, link, list, mentions, migrate, promote, reframe, remedy, resolve, surprise and wontfix, and `capture status --help` falls through to capture's own help. Bare `abcd capture` is what renders the ledger's status ('render the ledger's status bare'). A reader who types `abcd capture status` gets capture's lone-word refusal. The wording comes from the resolution text of iss-2610121653499543 (.abcd/work/issues/resolved/iss-2610121653499543-*.md), because the changelog is derived. Smallest fix: change 'capture status' to 'bare `capture`' in that record's resolution and re-derive the section.

failing.summary: commands/update.md:66 (raised by opus): Claim: the adr-38 network inventory says GitHub's attestations API and Sigstore's TUF repository are reached 'by `update`, to verify the build provenance'. The list reads as exhaustive. Reality: `ahoy install` now makes the same in-process check before it promotes a cached binary and on every owned PATH copy (internal/core/ahoy/apply.go:187 and :1620; commands/ahoy.md:468-473; docs/how-to/install.md:117-122). It also reaches GitHub's git API to resolve the tag's commit (internal/core/update/provenance.go:198, `git/ref/tags/<tag>`), which this inventory omits for both verbs. A user who relies on the inventory to know which verbs go online is not told that `ahoy install` does. Smallest fix: 'GitHub's attestations and git APIs and Sigstore's TUF repository by `update` and `ahoy install`, to verify the build provenance'.

failing.summary: docs/how-to/install.md:58 (raised by opus): Claim (also CHANGELOG.md:13 and README.md:103-110): with 'a `gh` that is not signed in, the download installs on the checksum alone' with a warning. Reality: in every path, a gh that has `--source-digest` first resolves the release's commit through the unauthenticated GitHub API, and refuses when that lookup fails, before gh's sign-in state is ever tested. The paths are hooks/bootstrap.sh (`elif [ "$release_sha" = unknown ]; then refuse ...`, in the 7b block), site-src/install.sh.tmpl:168-169 (`die "the commit of the latest release could not be resolved..."`) and both one-liners (`... || { echo "abcd install: the commit of the latest release could not be resolved ..."; exit 1; }`). So a signed-out gh behind an API rate limit or outage gets a refusal, not the documented checksum-only install. It fails closed and the message says to retry, so it does not lead to an unsafe action. Smallest fix: add to install.md and the changelog line 'provided GitHub's API names the release's commit; when it cannot, nothing is installed whether or not gh is signed in'.
